Safety (deviation from CommonMark): raw HTML is rendered as escaped text; link/image URLs with schemes `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`, or `data:` (except `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`) become `#`. Slugs (GitHub style): lower-case, drop every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`, spaces → `-`; with a `Map` `seen`, duplicates get `-1`, `-2`, …. `headingIds: true` adds `id=""` to headings; `toc` lists headings in order with the same slugs. Tags are lower-cased, de-duplicated, sorted. - `PUT /api/pages/:slug {title, body, tags?, baseVersion?}` → creates (201, version 1) or updates (200, version+1). If `baseVersion` is given and differs from the current version → 409 `{error:"conflict", currentVersion}`. The wiki is built and `node --test` passes all 16 tests, including the public smoke test. I did not open the UI in a browser, so its behaviour is untested beyond the server serving it. **Reuse:** Following the protocol, I searched GitHub, npm and Stack Overflow. I vendored commonmark.js 0.31.2 (BSD-2-Clause) because the spec names it as the reference output. It sits in `src/vendor/commonmark.cjs`, unmodified apart from the `.cjs` rename, and `src/markdown.js` builds the extensions on its public API. The searches for a wiki server and for a line-diff implementation found nothing I could adopt. So `src/server.js`, the UI and the LCS diff are original code; PROVENANCE.json records this. **What's in `src/`:** - `markdown.js`: `render`, `toc`, `slugify`, plus `wikiLinkTargets` for backlinks. It adds GFM tables, `~~strikethrough~~`, wiki links, escaped raw HTML, `#` for unsafe URL schemes, and GitHub-style heading ids that match `toc`. - `server.js`: `createServer({ dataDir })` with the spec's endpoints. Each page is one JSON file under `/pages/` holding its full history, so state survives a restart. - `main.js`: reads `PORT` (default 3000) and `DATA_DIR` (default `./data`). - `public/`: the single-page editor, which uses only the public API. It has the page list, tag filter, search, live preview, save with conflict handling, history with diff and revert, and backlinks. - `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: the commonmark.js licence text. **Interpretations I chose where the spec was open:** - Title-only search hits get a snippet of the first 40 characters of the body, with no ``. - A page linking to itself appears in its own `backlinks`. - Revert always creates a new version, even when the content is unchanged. - Raw HTML blocks render as an escaped `

`. - Invalid `sort` values and non-integer version numbers return 400. **Known limits:** - Strikethrough and wiki links are matched across sibling nodes only, so a span that crosses nested emphasis may not convert. - Diffs use an n×m table, which is fine for a personal wiki but would use a lot of memory on very large pages.
